1668.t: From γράφω (grắphō, “to write”) + -μα (-mă, result noun suffix).

1673.t: Adverb from εὐθύς (euthús, “straight”) + -ως (-ōs), using the stem εὐθε- (euthe-).

1683.t: Traditionally derived from a Proto-Indo-European *maǵʰ- (“to fight”), though Beekes considers Pre-Greek origin more likely. See also Old Armenian մաքառիմ (makʻaṙim, “to combat, quarrel”), which may continue the same root.

1602.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *kʰrūsós, cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀓𐀬𐀰 (ku-ru-so); further borrowed from a Semitic source, usually assumed to be Phoenician/Punic; compare Phoenician 𐤇𐤓𐤑 (ḥrṣ), Biblical Hebrew חָרוּץ (ḥārûṣ), Akkadian 𒆬𒄀 (ḫurāṣum).

1693.t: From ψάλλω (psállō, “to touch sharply, to pluck, to pull, to twitch”) + -τήριον (-tḗrion), from ψάω (psáō, “to touch lightly, to rub”), which acquired the meaning of plucking a harp, and later making music in general.

1663.t: Traditionally derived as a u-stem o-grade adjective of Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱ- (“sharp”) and compared with ὄκρις (ókrĭs, “point, prominence”); however, such a stem and ablaut combination is rather strange.

1662.t: PIE word *h₁nómn̥ From ὄνομα (ónomă, “name”) + -άζω (-ázō, denominative verb suffix).

1655.t: From Proto-Hellenic *elaíwā (whence also Mycenaean Greek 𐀁𐀨𐀷 (e-ra-wa)). Probably a borrowing from a Mediterranean Pre-Greek source, which may also be the source of Old Armenian եւղ (ewł, “oil”).

1691.t: García-Ramón suggests that the term is cognate with Vedic Sanskrit पा (pā, “to rise against, be hostile”) and Hittite [script needed] (pippa-, “to overturn”), and reconstructs Proto-Indo-European *(s)peh₂- (“to draw, set in motion”).

1645.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʷʰónos (“murder”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷʰónos (“killing, slaughter”). Equal to θείνω (theínō, “to strike”) + -ος (-os).

1600.t: Adjectival formation in -λός (-lós) from Proto-Indo-European *dʰewbʰ- (“deep, hazy, foggy”). Cognates include Old Irish dub (“dark”), Old English deaf (English deaf), Albanian dudum.

1620.t: From the root of γιγνώσκω (gignṓskō, “to know”) + -στός (-stós). A later variant form of γνωτός (gnōtós).

1684.t: Uncertain. The term has traditionally been compared to ἀμύμων (ămū́mōn, “blameless”), though Beekes rejects this proposal, arguing that the ablaut variation of ω ~ υ (ō ~ u) is impossible.

1646.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰey- Proto-Indo-European *-ōm Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰéyōm Proto-Hellenic *kʰiṓn Ancient Greek χιών From Proto-Hellenic *kʰiṓn, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰéyōm.

1665.t: From ὑποδέω (hupodéō, “to bind underneath”) + -μα (-ma) (these were fastened to the feet with straps).

1677.t: From κατα- (kata-, “downwards”) + φρονέω (phronéō, “to think, to be arrogant”).

1676.t: From κατακλύζω (kataklúzō, “to wash off, wash away, deluge, inundate”) (from Proto-Indo-European *ḱlewH- (“clean”)) + -μός (-mós), equivalent to κατα- (kata-) + κλυσμός (klŭsmós).

1634.t: From μετα- (metă-, prefix indicating change) + νοέω (noéō, “perceive by the eyes, observe”).

1601.t: From Proto-Hellenic *térpō, from Proto-Indo-European *terp- (“to satisfy”), cognate with German dürfen (“to need”) and obsolete and dialectal British English tharf (“to need”).

1695.t: From ἀνατίθημι (anatíthēmi, “to dedicate”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

1690.t: From Proto-Indo-European *(s)kel- (“crooked”), the same root of Latin scelus (“curse”), German scheel (“squinting”), Dutch scheel and Albanian çalë (“lame”).

1657.t: From ἐπι- (epĭ-, “on, onto”) + λέγω (légō, “to choose, to say”).

1644.t: Of unknown origin. Traditionally compared with Lithuanian spingė́ti, spingiù (“to glitter”), as well as with Old High German funko (“spark”), but this suggestion is impossible in view of the initial stops.

1696.t: Perhaps from a Proto-Indo-European *h₂pelH- (“to speak publicly”), and related via this root to Latvian pel̂t (“to revile”).

1611.t: The verb is clearly related to Old Armenian եփեմ (epʻem, “to boil, cook”) (whence modern Armenian եփել (epʻel)).

1628.t: From the root of κόπτω (kóptō, “to beat, strike, cut”) + -άζω (-ázō).

1608.t: From ἑπτά (heptá, “seven”) + -άκις (-ắkĭs, suffix for adverb of repetition).

1618.t: From αἱρετός (hairetós, “chosen, to be chosen”) (from αἱρέω (hairéō, “to grasp”)) + -ίζω (-ízō).

1643.t: From Proto-Hellenic *tʰrupʰā́, from the root of θρύπτω (thrúptō, “to shatter; to be wanton”) (from *tʰrúpʰyō.
